subsystems.name: Sorbent material
subsystems.role: captures water vapour from air even at low humidity.
parts: alternative porous sorbents such as silica gel or zeolites

subsystems.name: Sorbent bed
subsystems.role: holds the sorbent in a shape that air can flow through and heat can reach.

subsystems.name: Solar thermal collector
subsystems.role: provides the low-grade heat that releases water from the sorbent.

subsystems.name: Condenser
subsystems.role: cools the released vapour back into liquid water.

subsystems.name: Air handling
subsystems.role: moves ambient air through the sorbent during capture and removes humid air during release.

subsystems.name: Water collection and treatment
subsystems.role: stores and makes the water safe to drink.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the sorbent
buildSteps.detail: A metal salt and an organic linker are dissolved in solvent, heated to form MOF crystals, then washed and dried to activate the pores.

buildSteps.title: Form the sorbent into a usable shape
buildSteps.detail: The powder is pressed into pellets or coated onto metal fins so air can pass through without excessive pressure drop.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the sorbent bed
buildSteps.detail: The shaped sorbent is packed into a cartridge or bonded to a heat exchanger that can be heated and cooled cyclically.

buildSteps.title: Build the solar collector
buildSteps.detail: An absorber plate, glazing and insulation are assembled to heat a fluid or the sorbent bed directly using sunlight.

buildSteps.title: Build the condenser and tank
buildSteps.detail: A cooled surface and drip tray are placed downstream of the bed, connected to a collection tank and pump.

buildSteps.title: Integrate airflow and controls
buildSteps.detail: Fans, valves and a controller are wired to alternate between adsorption (air through the bed) and desorption (heat, then condense).

buildSteps.title: Test in low-humidity conditions
buildSteps.detail: The unit is run through many cycles at relative humidity below 30% to measure water yield per kilogram of sorbent per day.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Units are installed off-grid or in water-stressed areas, with filters replaced and sorbent regenerated or replaced after many cycles.

prerequisites.why: MOFs are made in laboratories and some industrial quantities, but low-cost, high-volume production is still developing.
They supply the 60–80 °C heat needed to release water without using electricity.
Cooling surfaces, filtration and disinfection are well-established technologies.

prerequisites.tech: Durable sorbents for many thousands of cycles
prerequisites.why: Some MOFs degrade after repeated heating and humid exposure; longer-lived materials are still being tested.
Off-grid operation needs efficient air movement and water pumping, often powered by a small solar panel.

pathway.milestone: pilot units in desert and arid regions producing a few litres per day per kilogram of sorbent
pathway.unlocks: proof that adsorption-based harvesting works at low humidity without grid power.

pathway.milestone: sorbents with higher water uptake and lower regeneration temperature
pathway.unlocks: more water per unit and smaller, cheaper devices.

pathway.milestone: continuous solar-powered operation with thermal storage
pathway.unlocks: day-and-night water production for households and small communities.

pathway.milestone: mass manufacturing of MOF-based harvesters at costs comparable to other off-grid water sources
pathway.unlocks: widespread deployment in water-stressed regions as a supplementary drinking-water supply.
